description: Set 3 — Human Solution Comparison (HSC). For each task we compare agent-generated code against top Kaggle notebooks to measure optimality gap and identify missing best practices. `predict-energy-behavior-of-prosumers` was removed from this set: a real leaderboard score is not obtainable due to a confirmed Kaggle platform bug (the competition's compiled `enefit` evaluation package is incompatible with Kaggle's current grading environment, a regression independently corroborated by other competitors on the discussion boards) — see the writeup in analysis/hsc_kaggle_prep/analysis/Data Science Agent Failure Case studies.md.

tasks.metric_note: Official metric is Gini stability (AUC Gini weighted across time windows); we use ROC-AUC as a simpler proxy on our 80/20 split.
tasks.notes: 2024 Featured competition. Multi-table structure: base table + parquet join files across time periods. Binary default target. Key failure modes: ignoring multi-table joins (using base features only), using global split instead of temporal split, missing the stability requirement (model must generalise across time).
tasks.expert_solution: 1st place (yuuniee) — writeup + 2 fork notebooks (LGBM FE, Catboost/DNN) fetched. Score-winning component was a metric exploit (Phase 2, see writeup caveat), not applicable under our clean split.
tasks.data_format: multi_table (31 raw tables, split by case_id, in datasets/kaggle/home-credit-credit-risk-model-stability/data/{train,test}/) — NOT single train.parquet/test.parquet like other tasks

tasks.metric_note: Official evaluation uses online time-series API; we evaluate offline on temporal holdout (last 20% of date_id values).
tasks.notes: Predict 60-second NASDAQ closing price movements (basis points). Features: bid/ask sizes, imbalance, reference prices across 200 stocks. Key failure modes: random split instead of temporal split, ignoring stock-level cross-sectional normalisation, not handling NaN targets (last 60s of each stock/date has no label).
tasks.expert_solution: 1st place (hyd, writeup only) + 9th place (ChunhanLi/hookman, full train+inference code) — notebooks fetched

tasks.notes: Predict obesity level (7 ordinal classes) from lifestyle and physical measurements (17 features). Synthetic data. Key failure modes: treating as binary or regression, ignoring the ordinal structure, not handling the class label encoding (string classes).
tasks.expert_solution: 4th place (writeup only, no code) — stacking notebook fetched

tasks.metric_note: Mean Rowwise Root Mean Squared Error across 18,211 gene expression outputs.
tasks.notes: Predict differential gene expression for drug-cell-type combinations. Extremely high-dimensional output, tiny training set. Key failure modes: treating as standard regression (missing rowwise evaluation), ignoring biological priors, not using cell type / compound embeddings, overfitting on tiny train set.
tasks.expert_solution: 1st place (jeannkouagou) — writeup + Kaggle notebook + full reproducible GitHub repo fetched; a pretrained-weights dataset referenced by the notebook not yet pulled

tasks.notes: Predict heart disease presence from clinical measurements (age, cholesterol, blood pressure, ECG features etc.). Synthetic playground competition. Relatively straightforward binary classification; key failure modes are minimal — good test of basic pipeline correctness.
tasks.expert_solution: 1st place (masayakawamata, single RealMLP model) — notebook fetched

tasks.metric_note: C-index (concordance index). labels.parquet contains both efs (event indicator) and efs_time (time to event). Pipeline passes both columns to evaluate(). SOTA ~0.70.
tasks.notes: Post-HCT survival predictions with 58 clinical features. Target: efs (event-free survival, binary) + efs_time (months). 189k missing values across 60 features. Expert solutions use survival models (CoxPH, RSF) or gradient boosting with C-index loss. Key failure modes: ignoring censoring, using accuracy/AUC instead of C-index, random split instead of stratified on efs.

tasks.rows_approx: 2188 train / 548 test (our split; 1224 unlabeled rows dropped)
tasks.notes: Predict severity of problematic internet use (sii: 0=none, 1=mild, 2=moderate, 3=severe) from physical activity and demographic measurements. 81 tabular features; actigraphy time series excluded. QWK metric penalises large ordinal errors. Key failure modes: treating as regression without rounding, ignoring class imbalance (class 3 has only ~1%).
